Area.evidence_source: [page/5/Text/18] his own life. He lived alone, far away from his family, and had become increasingly isolated and depressed. Although she was not fully aware of his struggle with drug addiction, or that it had recently caused him to lose his job, the mother was clearly concerned about his mental health. [page/5/Text/19] This example illustrates the difficulty of interpreting indirect suicide communications and the way in which the avoidance of open dialogue, through the use of face-saving devices such as euphemisms, hints and equivocations, retractions and denials, can obstruct intervention. However, on another level the mutual commitment to obfuscation may have arisen because the idea of suicidal distress and an associated feeling of hopelessness were too awful to share between mother and son 'on-record'.
